text:
marta (PM): Quick check-in — we're getting repeated asks: EU data residency + predictable p95 for enterprise customers. I sketched a phased roadmap; want pushback.

ton (infra): Phased sounds right. Three lanes: shared, reserved, tenant-isolated. Reserved pools easiest operationally, isolated needs infra changes + KMS.

kevin (eng): Agree. Big engineering work is predicate-based routing and the per-tenant config store. Also need model-aware routing to meet p95 targets.

sara (architect): Suggest we ship routing policy templates first (region preference, residency predicate, fallback behavior). Then allow per-tenant overrides. Isolated lanes last. Keeps blast radius small.

ben (sales): Customers insist on explicit fallback behavior in contract: either strict fail (reject) or degrade to lower-cost model. They also want clear upgrade path from shared->reserved->isolated.

viv (cs): For pilots we need audit logs + proof of key management. Two pilot customers already requiring KMS + audit streaming. Also request that audit gaps < 60s.

marta (PM): Draft launch criteria: pilot customers (2) onboarded; p95 < 300ms for reserved on 0-512 tokens; per-tenant policy overrides live; audit logs + KMS for isolated lane pilots; soft-eviction playbook + rollback < 5m. Thoughts?

kevin (eng): p95 bound depends heavily on model and token length. Recommend we scope perf SLAs to route+model bucket (e.g., short prompts 0-512, medium 512-2048). Need example prompt mixes for testing.

sara (architect): Example routing policy snippet for discussion:
```yaml
policies:
  - id: eu_residency
    match: request.customer.residency == "EU"
    prefer: region: eu-west-1
    fallback: region: usa-west-2
    fallback_policy: conditional_on_capacity
  - id: fail_or_degrade
    match: request.customer.fallback_mode == "degrade"
    action: route_to: model_variant: cheaper-q4
```

ton (infra): Note: fallback must check capacity headroom before routing; otherwise fallbacks will amplify SLO breaches. We'll add a gating threshold.

ben (sales): Can per-tenant fallback_mode be set at contract sign? We should support config in the tenant profile.

marta (PM): Yes. Roadmap proposal (high level):
- Q1: routing policy templates + baseline telemetry + example perf tests
- Q2: per-tenant overrides + canary routing tool
- Q3: reserved pools + SLA language + pilot recruitment
- Q4: tenant-isolated lanes + KMS + audit streaming (pilots)

viv (cs): Please include acceptance test: audit completeness with <60s gaps and end-to-end KMS proof.

kevin (eng): Engineering estimate: predicate DSL, metrics schema, per-tenant config store, and canary shaper across 6-9 sprints if parallel teams.

sara (architect): Also propose a simulation harness to estimate cost delta shared->reserved->isolated given traffic mixes; I'll prototype a small tool.

marta (PM): Actions: sara to prototype sim harness by next Tue; kevin to post metrics schema + test mixes; ton to draft capacity gating + soft-eviction playbook; ben/viv to surface pilot contacts and legal asks. ops-bot: created ticket PROD-4032 assigned to marta.

ben (sales): I'll loop in legal on fallback language.

marta (PM): If no other blockers I'll make a short PRD and schedule a 30m sync. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
